questions.question: As per the Rigvedic or Early Vedic Period (1500-1000 BC), who among the following was a River Goddess?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sindhu .__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sindhu**
 
• The Sindhu River, also referred to as the** Indus River** is a major waterway in South Asia.**
 One of the longest rivers in the world, the Sindhu has a total length of over** 2,000 miles **and runs **south from the Kailash Mountain** in **Tibet **all the way to the** Arabian Sea in Karachi, Pakistan**.

 It is the most important supplier of water resources to the** Punjab and Sindh plains** , it forms the backbone of agriculture and food production in Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Agni River**

 
 
• Agni River is a stream in **Madhya Pradesh**. 
 
• Agni River is situated nearby to **Chhota Tawa River,** and** northeast of Madni Reserved Forest.**
 
 
 
• The Rigvedic period, **also known as the** Early Vedic period, **is the first stage, while the Later Vedic period is the second. 
 
 
• The production of the** Rigvedic hymns** relates to the age of the** Early Vedic era.** 
 
• This date is estimated to be **between 1500 and 1000 BC. **
 
• **Between 1000 and 600 BC, **the later Vedic era occurs**.**
 
• The country of** seven rivers,** is mentioned in the** Rig Veda**.
 
• This comprises the** Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej rivers in Punjab, **as well as the** Indus** and **Saraswathi rivers.**

questions.question: Who among the following was the most important god of the Aryans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indra was the most important god of the Vedic Aryans and was considered the king of the gods.
 
• He was primarily known as the god of rain, thunder, and war, and was often invoked for victory in battles.
 
• Indra is frequently mentioned in the Rigveda, one of the oldest sacred texts of the Aryans, with over 250 hymns dedicated to him.
 
• He played a crucial role in Aryan mythology, often depicted as slaying the serpent Vritra, a symbol of drought, to release the waters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agni**

 
 
• Agni was another prominent deity of the Aryans, known as the god of fire.
 
• He acted as a mediator between the gods and humans, carrying offerings to the gods through fire.
 
• Agni played a vital role in Vedic rituals and sacrifices.
 
 
 
• **Pashupatinath**
 
 
• Pashupatinath is a form of Lord Shiva, a major deity in later Hinduism, but not prominent in early Aryan worship.
 
• The deity is revered as the lord of animals and is particularly worshipped in Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Marut**
 
 
• Maruts were storm deities, often associated with Indra in the Rigveda.
 
• They were considered the sons of Rudra and were known for their fierce nature and thunderous power.

questions.question: What is the collection of Vedic hymns or ‘mantras’ called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samhita**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Samhita**

 
 
• Samhita refers to the most ancient layer of Vedic texts, consisting of hymns, prayers, incantations, and sacrificial formulas addressed to various deities.
 
• These collections of mantras form the core of each of the four Vedas: Rigveda Samhita, Samaveda Samhita, Yajurveda Samhita, and Atharvaveda Samhita.
 
• The Rigveda Samhita is the oldest and most important, containing over a thousand hymns organized into ten books (mandalas). These hymns praise deities like Indra, Agni, Varuna, and Surya.
 
• The Samaveda Samhita consists primarily of melodies and chants derived from the Rigveda, arranged for liturgical purposes and musical recitation during Soma sacrifices.
 
• The Yajurveda Samhita contains prose mantras and sacrificial formulas used by priests to guide the rituals and offerings during yajnas (sacrifices). It exists in two recensions: Shukla (white) and Krishna (black).
 
• The Atharvaveda Samhita is distinct in its content, including spells, charms, healing incantations, and philosophical speculations, reflecting the daily life and concerns of the Vedic people alongside more esoteric knowledge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Smriti**

 
 
• Smriti literally means "that which is remembered" and refers to a vast body of post-Vedic Hindu texts considered secondary in authority to the Shrutis (the Vedas).
 
• Smriti literature encompasses a wide range of subjects, including law (Dharmashastras like Manusmriti), epics (Ramayana and Mahabharata), Puranas (mythological and encyclopedic texts), and various Sutras and Shastras on different aspects of dharma and practice.
 
• These texts, while revered and influential, are considered to be of human origin and thus subject to interpretation and change over time, unlike the divinely revealed Shrutis.
 
• Smriti texts provide detailed guidelines for social customs, legal procedures, ethical conduct, and religious practices, adapting Vedic principles to evolving societal contexts.
 
• The Smriti tradition plays a crucial role in shaping Hindu law, ethics, and social norms, and its diverse texts continue to be studied and interpreted in contemporary times.
 
 
 
• **Shruti **
 
 
• Shruti means "that which is heard" and refers to the body of Hindu religious texts considered to be of divine origin, revealed to ancient sages (rishis) through direct hearing.
 
• The Shrutis primarily consist of the four Vedas (Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda) and their associated Brahmanas, Aranyakas, and Upanishads.
 
• These texts are regarded as the foundational scriptures of Hinduism, possessing the highest religious authority and considered eternal truths.
 
• The Vedas contain hymns, rituals, philosophical insights, and spiritual knowledge, forming the basis of Vedic religion and subsequent Hindu traditions.
 
 
 
• **Upanishads**
 
 
• The Upanishads, the concluding part of the Vedas, delve into profound philosophical concepts about the nature of reality, the self (atman), and the ultimate reality (Brahman), laying the groundwork for Vedanta philosophy.
 
• Upanishad literally means "sitting near devotedly" and refers to a collection of philosophical texts that form the concluding part of the Vedas (Vedanta).
 
• These texts contain profound spiritual and philosophical teachings, exploring the nature of reality, the self, the relationship between the individual soul (atman) and the universal soul (Brahman), and the path to liberation (moksha).
 
• The Upanishads are primarily concerned with knowledge and wisdom, moving beyond the ritualistic focus of the earlier Vedic texts.
 
• Key concepts like karma, reincarnation, and the illusory nature of the material world are extensively discussed in the Upanishads.
 
• Major Upanishads like the Isha, Katha, Kena, Mundaka, and Chandogya are highly influential and have shaped the course of Indian philosophy and spirituality for centuries.

questions.question: Manuscripts were usually written on ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**palm leaf.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Manuscripts were usually written on **palm leaf.**
 
• Palm-leaf manuscripts are manuscripts made out of** dried palm leaves**.
 
• Or on the specially prepared **bark of a tree known as the birch,** which grows in the Himalayas, while inscriptions were engraved either on a stone surface or on bricks or metals.
 
• **Birch trees** are usually found in montane forests which are found in high altitude areas.
 
• Birch trees are trees that can grow on the highest altitudes among trees at typically more than** 3500 meters above sea level.**
 
• In India, they can only be seen in the **Himalayan region.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Manuscripts **were written on varied subjects such as religious beliefs and practices, the lives of kings, medicine, and science.
 
• Besides, there were epics, poems, musical dance dramas, and plays. 
 
• Manuscripts are found in hundreds of different languages and scripts.
 
 
• Often, one language is written in a number of different scripts.
 
• For example, Sanskrit is written in Oriya script, Grantha script, Devanagari script, and many other scripts.
 
 

 
• India possesses an estimated five million manuscripts, probably the largest collection in the world.
 
• The **Spitzer Manuscript **is the oldest surviving philosophical manuscript in Sanskrit.
 
• The **oldest manuscript** in the world is** The Pseudo-Apuleius Herbarium, dating back to the 6-7th century.**
